independence_declaration.statement: qa-verifier authored no product implementation in the DG2 scope. Its only authored files are QA tests, harnesses and evidence (tests/qa/**, e2e/**, docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/qa/**). The round-11 repair (D-071, T-DG2-BE16 258b7e5) is by backend-workflow-engineer. Every result here comes from qa-verifier's own runs in two disposable clones of 309aff2 (the round-11 freeze on top of source cbdb4f68) under $TMPDIR, removed afterwards. At the start HEAD was 309aff2 and the recomputed candidate ID matched (547 files) in the tree and in the clone. During the run HEAD moved to a7cdd7d through the other reviewers' auto-committed round-11 evidence; qa-verifier did not open those files. At the end the candidate ID was still 23e6c0a2... with 547 files (00-candidate-end.log). The verdict was formed without reading any other reviewer's round-11 record.

checks_run.command: e2e/support/qa-stack.sh npx playwright test e2e/dg2-qa-r11.spec.ts (inside the QA-R11-17 run)
checks_run.environment: as QA-R11-17; chromium-en and chromium-ar; both locale settings (4 executions)
checks_run.expected: Exactly one 413 evidence.too_large each time. When the body was not completely received: Connection: close, and the server closes the socket within 3 s (not ~65 s). Nothing stored, no audit row, version unchanged, readyz 200.
checks_run.actual: All 4 executions passed. (a) 413 Connection: close; server FIN +0 ms, socket closed about 500 ms after the response (the designed RST-avoidance linger); the client's later write got EPIPE. (b)-(e) 413 Connection: close; server FIN and close within 0-1 ms of the response. (f) The whole 25 MiB + 1 body had arrived before the answer, so the 413 kept the connection (Connection: keep-alive), per BE16 policy 3. I checked that this connection is not held or paused: a following GET /me on the same socket answered 200 in about 21 ms. In every execution: evidence version 1 -> 1, currentContentId null, 0 content rows, 0 stored files, the item's audit rows 1 -> 1 (the create only), readyz 200. My first dry run of the spec (not counted) expected Connection: close for case (f) as well and failed only on that assertion. That was my over-strict expectation, not a defect: the server answered 413 and kept a healthy connection whose next request was served. I corrected the spec to check that the kept connection serves a next request.

checks_run.procedure: R11-02 starts a separate API process from the same build (apps/api/dist/main.js, own port, LOG_LEVEL=info). (a) It holds an idle keep-alive socket after GET /me 200, a stalled over-limit chunked upload (413) and a fully-sent 25 MiB + 1 upload (413), then sends SIGTERM (main.ts -> app.close()). (b) A new process gets an under-limit upload stalled in flight (2 MiB of a declared 10 MiB, no response yet), then SIGTERM.
checks_run.command: (inside the QA-R11-17 run) spawn node apps/api/dist/main.js; kill -TERM
checks_run.expected: (a) exit 0 within 3 s, every socket closed, 'shut down' logged. (b) exit 0 within the 5 s grace + margin (< 8 s), the stalled socket closed by the server, nothing stored.
checks_run.actual: (a) SIGTERM -> exit 0 in 19-370 ms. All three sockets were closed and 'shut down' was logged. (b) SIGTERM -> exit 0 in 5025-5034 ms. The stalled socket was closed about 5005 ms after SIGTERM, the 'grace period elapsed' warning was logged, and the stalled socket got no response. 0 content rows, 0 stored files; the shared stack stayed ready (200). The auditor's ~65 s app.close() stall did not reproduce.

checks_run.procedure: R11-03 raw-socket uploads: 1 MiB random + all 256 byte values with Content-Length; 1 MiB random + all 256 byte values + CRLF '0' CRLF bytes, chunked in odd 77,777-byte chunks; exactly 25 MiB (the boundary). Then 25 MiB + 1 chunked. Download each revision and compare it with the DB and the Digest header.
checks_run.expected: 200 for each of the three uploads; downloaded bytes equal the sent bytes; sha256 = DB = Digest; one audit row each. 25 MiB + 1: 413, nothing changes.
checks_run.actual: All 4 executions passed. 1,049,088 B, 1,048,837 B and 26,214,400 B were each answered 200, downloaded byte-exact, with sha256 equal in the DB row and the Digest header, and 1 audit row each. 25 MiB + 1 chunked: 413 evidence.too_large. The body had arrived completely, so the connection was kept, and the next GET /me on it answered 200. Content rows 3 -> 3, version 4 -> 4.

summary: PASS on candidate 23e6c0a2 (547 files, source cbdb4f68). Full regression in both locale settings: static checks; unit 7/7 runs (771 each); integration 6/6 runs (623 each, with every assigned file green); product e2e 64/64 and qa-stack e2e 118/118 per setting; axe 636 scans with 0 serious or critical. New raw-socket checks for BE16: every over-limit upload, chunked or Content-Length and fully sent or stalled, gets exactly one 413. When the body is incomplete, the server closes the connection within about 0.5 s instead of ~65 s. When the over-limit body arrived in full, the connection is kept and serves the next request. Nothing is stored and nothing is audited. SIGTERM -> app.close() exits in under 0.4 s after a refused upload, and in about 5.03 s (the grace period) with an upload stalled in flight. Binary uploads up to exactly 25 MiB are stored byte-exact (sha256 = DB = Digest). A keep-alive socket survives 200/409/201 responses, and Arabic/emoji text round-trips verbatim. The R8-05/R9-05 messages are each shown once. Unmatched routes are rate-limited. One new Low, non-mandatory finding: F-DG2-430, a pre-existing React setState-in-render warning in the unit logs. Residuals D-057, D-058 and D-049 are PASS on the offline/config surface. No business approval is implied.
